topic.bc01-the-book.speaker: hulm-tei
topic.bc01-the-book.prompt: Tell me about the estate's debt book.
lines: Every line of the estate's debt book is true. Rows-For-Another's food is in it. So is the boat's upkeep, and her sick days. I name a buy-out by the book. I am a steward. I am not a slaver.
lines@low: Every line of the estate's debt book is true. Rows-For-Another's food is in it, and the boat's upkeep, and her sick days. I name a buy-out by the book. I am a steward, not a slaver.
lines@high: I will speak plainly, because you have listened. Every line of the estate's debt book is true. Rows-For-Another's food is in it. So is the boat's upkeep, and her sick days. I name a buy-out by the book. Nothing else sets it. Some call that slaving. I am a steward. I keep what is true.

topic.bc01-the-estate.speaker: never-sold
topic.bc01-the-estate.prompt: What do the Chainbreakers need done?
lines: Rows-For-Another took a boat from the estate north of Blackrose. She took it on an Owing of four months. An Owing is a debt paid in work. That was eleven years ago. She works it still. I have saved enough to buy out the Owing. Hulm-Tei, the steward, keeps the debt book in a locked chest on the landing. Take the swamp road north out of Blackrose. The landing is a short walk on, on the channel side, with boats at the water. I will meet you there. She talks of the channel after dark. It runs from the landing out of the estate's reach. She says she cannot drown in it. Bring me the book.

topic.bc01-bring-down.speaker: never-sold
topic.bc01-bring-down.prompt: I have the estate's debt book.
lines: That is the book. I will read her page. I do not argue the entries. I tear out her page and give it to her. Then I leave four months in coin in the steward's chest. That was the first price.
lines@low: That is the book. Stand back. I tear out her page and give it to her, and I leave four months in coin in the steward's chest. That was the first price.
lines@high: You have done what I could not. Give me the book. I will read her page. I do not argue the entries. I tear out her page and give it to her. Then I leave four months in coin in the steward's chest. That was the first price. It is paid. Rows-For-Another is free because of you.

topic.bc01-cut-loose.speaker: rows-for-another
lines: I will not wait on the book. Two estate men walk the landing at night. Past them, the channel runs out of the estate's reach. I cannot drown in it. Go first. I will follow you.
day: Not while the estate's men can see us. Come to me after dark, when none of them is looking.
